'''Emilio Baiada''' (also known as '''Emilio Bajada''');<ref name="Bajada">See for example {{harv|Cattelani Degani|2022|pp=2–3, 6, 22}}.</ref> (12 January 1914 – 14 May 1984) was an Italian [[mathematician]], working in mathematical analysis and the calculus of variation.<ref name="Vinti1984">See {{harv|Vinti|1984}}, {{harv|Vinti|2007}}, {{harv|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=64}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Baiada was born on 12 January 1914 in [[Tunis]]. He studied at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]] in [[Pisa]], where he graduated with highest honors in June 1937 along with [[Leonida Tonelli]],<ref name="graduation">{{harvtxt|Barbieri|1992|p=54}} reports that his doctoral examination was held on 4 July 1937.</ref> with whom he worked as an assistant from 1938 to 1941,<ref>{{harvtxt|Barbieri|1992|p=54}} simply states that Baiada was one Tonelli's pupils, while {{harvtxt|Nastasi|1996|p=923}} reports that Baiada classified first in the 1940 competitive exam for the chair of [[assistant professor]] of [[infinitesimal analysis]], followed respectively by [[Landolino Giuliano]] and [[Enzo Martinelli]]. {{harvtxt|Pepe|1987|p=313}} lists Baiada in the group of Tonelli's pupils doing research work on the calculus of variation, as also {{harvtxt|Ricci|1951|p=173}} does. Moreover, in a letter dated 28 July 1942 and published as {{harv|Baiada|1998}} Baiada himself informs Tonelli on his current situation and asks if he has received a previously compiled bibliography on [[operational calculus]].</ref> when he left for the war.<ref name="war">{{harvtxt|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=64}} reports that it was in 1940 that he was called to arms in the military aviation. Nevertheless, in a letter dated 28 July 1942 {{harv|Baiada|1998}} Baiada states that he received the official call to arms only about twelve days before.</ref> In 1945 he began to teach analysis, theory of functions, [[calculus]] and [[Classical mechanics|rational mechanics]] at the Scuola Normale. In 1948 he obtained a degree in Analysis; his [[Ph.D.]] thesis was written under the direction of Tonelli and [[Marston Morse]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|123173}}</ref>

In 1949 he went on leave from the University of Pisa and moved first to the [[University of Cincinnati]],<ref name="Cincinnati">See {{harv|Bulletin of the AMS|1950|p=272}}, {{harv|Vinti|1984|p=III}}, {{harv|Vinti|2007|p=908}}.</ref><ref name="AMSmeeting">{{harvtxt|Hollcroft|1950|pp=146–147}} writes that Baiada was elected to membership during the fifty-six Annual Meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]], on nomination of institutional members, specifically the University of Cincinnati: furthermore he writes that at the Meeting Baiada read the paper "An Isoperimetric Problem for Ship-Bodies" {{harv|Hollcroft|1950|pp=161}}, presented by C. N. Moore {{harv|Hollcroft|1950|pp=154}}.</ref> where he worked with scientists like [[Otto Szász]] and [[Charles Napoleon Moore]], and then to [[Princeton University]],<ref name="Princeton">See {{harv|Vinti|1984|p=III}}, {{harv|Vinti|2007|p=908}}, {{harvtxt|Mitchell|1980|p=58}}, {{harv|The Institute for Advanced Study|2012}}. {{harvtxt|Mitchell|1980|p=58}} states he stayed there in the years 1950 and 1951, while {{harv|The Institute for Advanced Study|2012}} is slightly more precise, saying that he worked at the institute from September 1950 to July 1951: other references are less detailed.</ref> where he worked with Morse.<ref>See {{harv|Morse|Baiada|1953}}, {{harv|Vinti|2007|p=908}} and {{harv|Vinti|1984|p=III}}.</ref>
In 1952 he obtained the chair of analysis of the [[University of Palermo]], where he taught until 1961 before transferring to the [[University of Modena]].<ref name="Modena1961">{{harv|Vinti|2007}}, {{harv|Cattelani Degani|2022|p=2}}.</ref> where he re-launched the Institute of Mathematics and developed its Library and Mathematical Seminar.<ref name="Barbieri">{{harvtxt|Barbieri|1992|p=54}} writes that</ref>

==Work==

===Institutional work===
Baiada was one of the leading forces behind the reprise in mathematical studies in Modena in the postwar period.<ref>According to what Silvio Cinquini writes in a letter to Francesco Barbieri, published by {{harvtxt|Cattelani Degani|2022|p=8}}:—"Cosicché se nei confronti della matematica I meriti di Bajada sono immensi, c'é da soggiungere che Bajada avrebbe potuto fare ancora di più, se l'Università di Modena lo avesse chiamato alcuni anni prima." (Free {{translation|:—"Thus, if Bajada's merits in the field of mathematics are immense, it should be added that Bajada could have accomplished even more had the University of Modena called him a few years earlier"}}).</ref> Teaching mathematical analysis in Modena from 1961,<ref name="Modena1961" /> he was director of the Institute of Mathematics of the university from the academic year 1962–63 to the 1966—67:<ref>{{harv|Cattelani Degani|Uccellari|1998|pp=103, 116}}.</ref> he promoted its 1966 dedication to [[Giuseppe Vitali]],<ref name="Vitali1966">{{harv|Cattelani Degani|2022|p=2}}, {{harv|Cattelani Degani|Uccellari|1998|p=114}}. Furthermore, according to {{harv|Caramagno|2014|p=55}}, in the archive of the [[Italian Mathematical Union]] at the Department of Mathematics of the University of Bologna, precisely in the Vitali funds, two letters written by Emilio Baiada from 1966 to 1968 to the Rector of the University of Modena are conserved. The first one is a request to have the Institute in Modena named after Vitali, while the second one is a request to remedy the omission of Vitali’s name in Carlo Guido Mor’s ''Storia dell'università di Modena'' ({{translation|''History of the University of Modena''}}, several editions).</ref> and was also behind the construction of the then new building for the department, which opened officially during the 1974–75 academic year.<ref>{{harv|Cattelani Degani|Uccellari|1998|p=114}}. Moreover {{harvtxt|Cattelani Degani|2022|loc=p. 2, footnote 5}} refers that Bajada started complaining to the Rector about the "dilapidated and highly inadequate condition of the institute" already in December 1962, as also Silvio Cinquini does in his letter {{harvtxt|Cattelani Degani|2022|p=6}}.</ref> Moreover, he held the direction of the direction of the Atti del Seminario Matematico e Fisico dell'Università di Modena from 1977 up to 1983.<ref>{{harv|Cattelani Degani|1998|pp=582–583}}, {{harv|Cattelani Degani|Uccellari|1998|pp=92, 103}}.</ref>

===Research activity===
He published more than 60 papers on differential equations, [[Fourier series]], series expansion of orthonormal functions, topology of varieties, real analysis, calculus of variations and on the theory of functions.<ref>{{harv|Vinti|2007}}.</ref>

===Teaching activity===
In 1961 he went from Palermo to Modena, teaching several mathematical analysis courses up to the year of his death.<ref>See {{harv|Cattelani Degani|Uccellari|1998|p=2}} for a complete list.</ref> {{harvtxt|Vinti|2007}} gives a complete list of Emilio Baiada's doctoral students.

==Honors==
Baiada won the Michel prize for the best thesis in Pisa,<ref name="MichelPrize"/> and the 1940 Merlani prize of the [[Accademia delle Scienze dell'Istituto di Bologna]] for "contributions on subjects of calculus of variations".<ref name="MerlaniPrize"/> During his stay in Palermo, from 1952 to 1961, he was elected corresponding member of the Accademia Nazionale di Scienze, Lettere e Arti di Palermo.<ref name="AccademiaPalermo">See {{harv|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=65}}.</ref> In 1967 he was elected [[corresponding member]] of the Accademia di Scienze, Lettere e Arti di Modena.<ref name="AccademiaModena">See {{harv|Vinti|1984|p=IV}}, {{harv|Vinti|2007}}, {{harv|Barbieri|1992|p=61}}, {{harv|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=64}}. The former references do not report the exact date of his election while the latter, particularly the last one (for obvious reasons) do.</ref> On 9 June 1976, he was awarded the Golden medal "[[Benemeriti della Scuola, della Cultura, dell'Arte]]" by the [[President of the Italian Republic]].<ref name="Benem"/><ref name="Benemeriti"/>
